question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.**
solution:
The correct answer is: **Spotted**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• '**spotted**' fits perfectly in the blank.
 
• It is the past participle of the verb "**spot**," which means to observe, detect, or notice something. (किसी चीज़ का निरीक्षण करना, पता लगाना या नोटिस करना)
 
• In the context of the sentence, it indicates that some of the moons were observed or detected in 2019.
 
• So, the correct option is "spotted," as it correctly conveys that the moons were observed in the past, specifically in 2019.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

Complete passage: *Astronomers have discovered 62 new moons orbiting the ringed planet Saturn. Though some of the moons had been (1) **spotted __**as early as 2019, it takes more than sighting an object close to a planet to (2) ________ it is a moon and not an asteroid making a brief close passage to that planet.*

*Performing a painstaking (3) **________ **of matching objects detected on different nights over the course of 24 months, the team tracked 63 objects that they ended up confirming as moons. One of (4) ________ satellites was revealed back in 2021, with the remaining 62 moons gradually announced over the past few weeks.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **spot**: This is the base form of the verb and does not fit grammatically in this context.
 
• **spotting**: This is the present participle form of the verb "spot." It describes an ongoing action, so it doesn't fit well in this sentence.
 
• **spots**: This is the present tense form of the verb "spot." It doesn't fit in this context because the sentence is discussing a past event.
